transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We need to get the wrap disposition plan locked today so we're clear for the Friday dismantling after the final stage shoot. Per our standard wrap meeting, each department lead needs to confirm the exact disposition and environmental-compliance requirements for their department. If anyone has an exception to the current draft plan — which sends scenic pieces to general salvage and places selected hero props in production storage — I need you to state the exact corrective requirement so it can be entered into the meeting record before I can approve. Let's start going through department by department.

transcript.text: I have an exception to the draft plan. The antique jukebox listed as a hero prop is actually a rental piece. I confirmed with the rental house yesterday that its agreement requires it to be returned to the owner in its original condition — it cannot go to production storage or salvage. The exact corrective requirement is: remove the antique jukebox from the hero-prop storage list and schedule its return to the rental house owner in original condition before Friday's dismantling.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have an exception to the draft plan. The current draft sends scenic pieces to a general salvage vendor, but our city green-film incentive requires at least 85 percent of dismantled set material by weight to be diverted from landfill. I confirmed with the approved vendor this morning that their audited plan reaches that threshold only through separate wood and metal recycling bins plus a certified transfer record. However, the compliance packet still contains the general-salvage draft. The exact corrective requirement is: replace the general-salvage vendor assignment for scenic pieces with the approved vendor's audited plan using separate wood and metal recycling bins plus a certified transfer record, and update the compliance packet to reflect this before the plan is locked.
